questions: Do you live in a house or an apartment?
What is your favourite room in your home? Why?
Is there anything you would like to change about your home?
Do you plan to live there for a long time?
What can you see from the windows of your home?
Do you work or are you a student?
What do you enjoy most about your work or studies?
Is there anything you find difficult about your work or studies?
What did you want to be when you were a child?
Would you like to change your job or subject in the future?
What do you like to do in your free time?
Have your hobbies changed since you were a child?
Do you prefer spending your free time alone or with other people?
Is there a new hobby you would like to try? Why?
What kind of food do you like to eat?
Do you prefer eating at home or eating out? Why?
Can you cook? Who taught you?
Are there any foods you disliked as a child but enjoy now?
Is food an important part of celebrations in your country?
Do you enjoy travelling?
What is the most interesting place you have visited?
Do you prefer travelling alone or with friends or family?
Is there a country you would especially like to visit? Why?
How often do you use the internet?
What do you mainly use your mobile phone for?
Is there any piece of technology you could not live without?
Did you use computers when you were at primary school?
Do you ever try to spend time away from screens?

part2.cueCard: Describe a person who has influenced you in an important way.
bullets: and explain why they have influenced you
followUp: Do you still see this person often?
Do you think you have influenced anyone yourself?

part2.cueCard: Describe a place you visited that made a strong impression on you.
bullets: and explain why it made such a strong impression on you
followUp: Would you like to go back there?
Have you recommended this place to other people?

part2.cueCard: Describe an object you own that is important to you.
bullets: and explain why it is important to you
followUp: Would you be upset if you lost it?
Do you think you will keep it for a long time?

part2.cueCard: Describe a celebration or event that you particularly enjoyed.
bullets: where and when it took place
and explain why you enjoyed it so much
followUp: Do you often attend events like this?
Is there an event you are looking forward to?

part2.cueCard: Describe a skill or activity you learned that has been useful to you.
bullets: what the skill or activity is
when and how you learned it
and explain why it has been useful to you
followUp: Would you recommend other people learn this skill?
Is there another skill you would like to learn?

part2.cueCard: Describe a film or television programme that you found particularly interesting.
bullets: when and where you watched it
and explain why you found it so interesting
followUp: Have you watched it more than once?
Do you usually watch this kind of programme?

questions: What qualities do you think make someone a good role model for young people?
Do you think celebrities have too much influence on society today?
In what ways do the people who influence us change as we get older?
Some people say parents are the most important influence in a child's life. Do you agree?
How might the role of teachers as influences change in the future?
Why do you think some places attract far more tourists than others?
What are the advantages and disadvantages of tourism for a local community?
Do you think people will still want to travel to see places in person when virtual experiences improve?
How can governments protect popular natural sites from being damaged by visitors?
Is it better to visit many places briefly or a few places in depth?
Why do people become emotionally attached to certain possessions?
Do you think modern society encourages people to buy more than they need?
How do attitudes towards material possessions differ between generations?
Some people believe experiences are more valuable than objects. What is your view?
How might our relationship with physical objects change as more things become digital?
Why are traditional celebrations important to a society?
Do you think festivals have become too commercialised in recent years?
How have the ways people celebrate special occasions changed over the past few decades?
Should governments spend public money on large national celebrations?
Do you think globalisation will make celebrations around the world more similar?
Which skills do you think will be most important for people in the future?
Is it easier to learn new skills as a child or as an adult? Why?
Do you think schools focus too much on academic knowledge and not enough on practical skills?
How has the internet changed the way people learn new skills?
Should employers be responsible for training their staff, or should individuals train themselves?
How do films and television influence people's views of other countries?
Do you think streaming services will completely replace cinemas one day?
Should there be stricter controls on what children can watch?
In what ways can films be used for education as well as entertainment?
Why do you think some films become internationally successful while others do not?
